GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No 4486 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.03.2025 
  
REDUCTION IN FUNDING FOR TRIBAL STUDENTS 
  
4486  SHRI SUDAMA PRASAD: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: - 
  
 (a) whether the Government has reduced funding for educational schemes aimed at tribal and 
minority students in the Union Budget 2025 and if so, the reasons therefor along with the manner 
in which the Government justifies such reductions;  
  
(b) the specific measures being taken to ensure that the education needs of tribal and minority 
students are not compromised despite the budget cuts;  
  
(c) the manner in which the Government is addressing the potential impact on access to quality 
education for these communities;  
  
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment on the effect of these budget cuts on 
the educational attainment of tribal and minority students and if so, the details and findings thereof; 
and  
  
(e) the alternative mechanisms implemented to support the education of tribal and minority 
students during the current financial year? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY)  
(a) to (e): Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the following Scholarship Schemes to 
promote and encourage basic and higher education amongst ST population.  
           i)     Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class IX and X) 
           ii)    Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above)          
           iii)  National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for STs 
            (a) National Fellowship for ST students (NFST) 
            (b) National Scholarship for Higher Education (Top Class) 
          iv)     National Overseas Scholarship for ST students. 
  
For the Centrally Sponsored Schemes(Sr no-i & ii) of Pre-Matric and Post-Matric 
Scholarship for ST students  ₹12516.70 crore was sanctioned for the Finance Commission Cycle 
from 2021-22 to 2025-26. However, total expenditure incurred by Ministry is ₹10577.91 crore till 
F.Y. 2024-25 (as on 24.03.2025). Thus, only Rs.1938.79 crore is available for FY 2025-26 and the 
Ministry has already initiated revised EFC proposal of an additional allocation of Rs.1983.67 crore 
for FY 2025-26 under Post-Matric Scholarship scheme for ST students. 

Further, for the Central Sector Schemes (Sr No. iii and iv) of National Fellowship and 
Scholarship for Higher Education and National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for ST students ₹755 
crore was sanctioned for the Finance Commission Cycle from 2021-22 to 2025-26. However, total 
expenditure incurred by Ministry is ₹756.95 crore till F.Y. 2024-25 (as on 24.03.2025). Notably, 
the Ministry has spent five-year budget within four years due to increase in number of scholars 
under National Scholarship (Top Class) being the open-ended scheme and enhancement of 
fellowship amount by UGC under National Fellowship. This has resulted in budget provision of 
less amount for FY 2025-26. To address the funding shortfall, the Ministry has already initiated 
revised EFC proposal for an additional allocation of ₹ 220 crore for FY 2025-26 under National 
Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students and  ₹9.95 crore under National 
Overseas Scholarship Scheme. 
Further, Ministry of Minority Affairs has intimated that it implements various schemes for socio-
economic empowerment of the six (6) centrally notified minority communities including various 
educational empowerment Schemes such as (i) Pre-Matric, (ii) Post-Matric and (iii) Merit-cum-
Means based scholarships which are implemented across the country covering rural as well as 
urban areas. The reason for reduction in the budget is attributed to the Right to Education (RTE) 
Act, 2009, which makes it obligatory for the Government to provide free and compulsory 
elementary education (classes I to VIII) to each and every child. Accordingly, Pre-Matric 
Scholarship Scheme has been restricted to students studying in classes IX and X. Similarly, 
considering the overlap of Maulana Azad National Fellowship and Padho Pardesh interest subsidy 
scheme for overseas studies, with similar schemes of other Ministries/ Departments, the schemes 
have been discontinued. Moreover, the schemes have not been approved for implementation for 
the year 2024-25. Therefore, the budget allocation in the Union Budget for 2025-26 has been 
reduced. 
Further, the Government has undertaken several steps to encourage education among the children 
of minority communities across the country for socio-economic and educational empowerment of 
the notified minority communities and as a result to reduce the dropout rate various scholarship 
schemes have been implemented, viz. Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme was approved in January 
2008 for class I-X and was applicable upto 2021-22, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme was 
launched in November 2007 for class XIth to Ph.D. and Merit-cum-Means based Scholarship 
Scheme was launched in the year 2007 for Technical and Professional Courses at under 
graduate/post graduate level. A very large number of students from minority communities have 
benefited through these programmes. In all these schemes, 30% Scholarships have been earmarked 
for girl students of minority community. So far, a total of 8.30 crore scholarships have been 
awarded to minority students. 
In addition, the Govt. has implemented various schemes for the welfare and upliftment of every 
strata, including minorities, especially the economically weaker and lesser privileged sections of 
the society, through schemes of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Ministry 
of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Textiles, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of Women 
and Child Development and Ministry of Rural Development.

TO BE ANSWERED ON- 27/03/2025 
  
ESTABLISHMENT OF EMRS IN DADRA AND NAGAR HAVELI 
†4487. SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to open new Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) to 
provide quality education to tribal students in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the total funds sanctioned for the establishment of EMRS in the districts of Dadra and 
Nagar Haveli during the current year; 
(d) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to promote tribal students in sports and provide a 
platform to enhance their capabilities; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to achieve the target of establishing 728 EMRS across the country 
by 2025-26? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI. DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a) to (c): In Union Budget of 2018-19, Government of India announced that to provide quality 
education to the tribal children in their own environment, Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) 
will be established in every block having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal 
persons (as per census 2011).  Ministry of Tribal Affairs has approved one EMRS in Union Territory 
of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The said EMRS is functional from 2020-21. hence no 
funds have been sanctioned for establishment of EMRS during the current year. 
(d): In order to encourage & promote sports activities in EMRSs, National Sports meet is organized. 
Participants are selected through State-level Sports Meets conducted in states where EMRSs are 
operational. Additionally, as part of the NTPC Dhanurvidya Project, archery centers are planned to be 
built in partnership with the Archery Association of India (AAI) to develop gifted archers and offer 
specialized instruction with an emphasis on getting them ready for the next Olympic Games. Further, 
Games facilities (indoor and outdoor) are provided in EMRSs and provision of archery range has also 
been made in all EMRSs being constructed under the new scheme. 
 

(e): Ministry of Tribal Affairs has undertaken several key measures to achieve the target of 
establishing 728 EMRS across the country by 2025-26 by taking the following steps: 
(1) Simplification of process by adopting the following measures by National Education Society 
for Tribal Students (NESTS) , an autonomous body under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to 
manage the EMRSs: 
(i)  The detailed structure covering all aspects of EMRS working have been    laid down. 
(ii)  Relaxation in provision of 15.00 acre land area for construction of EMRS. 
(iii) Approval process for Administrative approval, Expenditure sanction and   DPR have been 
streamlined. 
(iv)  Project wise Escrow Accounts have been opened to ensure that funds   are not diverted and 
available for the designated project only. 
(2) Regular Monitoring of  progress  at central level is done through NESTS and at the state level 
monitoring is done by the State Societies of State Tribal Departments. Further District Level Committee 
headed by the District Collector monitor the progress of EMRSs at district level. Additionally , Review 
meeting with construction agencies and coordination with state governments to expedite the progress 
and identify and allocate suitable land for construction of EMRS are held by NESTS and Ministry.  
 (3). Quality Monitoring:  
  
(i) National level workshop for Engineers engaged in construction of EMRSs work 
(ii) Engagement of reputed agencies i.e. CBRI Roorkee, IIT Roorkee for quality control of construction 
of EMRS.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 4488 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 27/03/2025 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF PM-JANMAN SCHEME 
  
4488. SHRI ADHIKARI SOUMENDU: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the work done under PM-JANMAN scheme to integrate tribal communities 
into the mainstream; 
  
(b) the details of its implementation including collaboration with the State Government and 
PVTG communities; 
  
(c) the details of the initiatives taken to support the PVTGs; and 
  
(d)  the steps taken to ensure effective execution and monitoring of the said scheme across the 
country? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY): 
  
(a) to (d): On 15th November 2023, Hon'ble Prime Minister launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati 
Adivasi Nyaya Maha AbhiyaN (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG 
communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities to 
improve their socio-economic conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and 
improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, 
electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. 
These objectives are being met through 11 interventions implemented by 9-line Ministries. 
  
In view of the implementation of PM JANMAN, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the 
State Governments/ UT Administration/departments has undertaken habitation level data 
collection exercise through PM Gati Shakti mobile application to estimate PVTG population 
figures and infrastructure gaps in order to cover PVTG population residing in villages & 
habitations under PM JANMAN. 
  
In coordination with State Governments, IEC camps have been organized which were aimed 
at facilitating in preparation of basic documents like Aadhar Card, Caste certificate, Jan Dhan 
bank account which are required for availing benefits under different schemes including 
Ayushman Card, PM Awas, MNREGA etc. 
  
Prior to launch of PMJANMAN, for development of PVTGs, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs 
was implementing scheme of “Development of PVTGs” wherein funds were provided to the 

concerned State Government / UT on the basis of their proposals for Conservation cum 
Development (CCD) plans. These were to fill gaps in infrastructure and were demand driven. 
With the introduction of PMJANMAN Scheme the Development of PVTG Scheme has been 
discontinued and Ministry is only providing committed liabilities till March 2025. 
  
Ministry of Tribal Affairs is also implementing a flagship scheme “Eklavya Model Residential 
School (EMRS)” to provide quality education to ST Students from class 6th to 12th. 5% seats 
in each of the EMRSs is reserved for PVTG students.   
  
In the scheme of National Fellowship, 25 slots out of 750 slots are reserved for PVTG students. 
Under National Overseas Scholarship for ST students, 3 slots out of 20 slots are reserved for 
PVTG candidate. 
  
To ensure the effective implementation of the PMJANMAN Scheme, the Ministry has 
established a Project Monitoring Unit at the national level. This unit regularly collaborates with 
partner ministries to assess progress. In addition, regular reviews are conducted by the Ministry 
with District Collectors, partner Ministries and State Tribal Welfare Departments through 
video conferences. Even Manthan Shivirs are held periodically at National level.

the 22 March 2025, the new edition of Jal Shakti Abhiyan was launched across the country 
themed “Peoples' Action for Water Conservation - Towards Intensified Community Connect” 
with special emphasis on 148 focus districts. The initiative promo tes water conservation, 
rainwater harvesting, and sustainable resource management through community participation 
and scientific interventions.

PROGRESS OF PMKSY IN TAMIL NADU 
4491.   SHRI MALAIYARASAN D 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sincha yee Yojana (PMKSY) – Har Khet Ko Pani and the 
progress made in ensuring water availability for irrigation through this scheme in Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the steps taken by the Government under the PMK SY to address the repair, renovation and restoratio n of 
water bodies in Tamil Nadu and the number of water bodies renovated or restored under this initiative; 
(c) the manner in which the financial assistance ha s been allocated to Tamil Nadu under the PMKSY – Ha r 
Khet Ko Pani for the restoration of water bodies and for improving irrigation infrastructure; 
(d) the specific impact of the repair and renovation of water bodies had on agricultural productivity and water 
availability for farmers in Tamil Nadu particularly in drought-prone and water-scarce regions; and 
(e) the measures put in place to ensure the long-te rm sustainability and maintenance of the renovated water 
bodies and irrigation systems in Tamil Nadu? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) to (d)    A total of 545 water bodies across Phases I to VII I in Tamil Nadu have been taken up under the 
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana- Har Khet Ko  Pani  (PMKSY-HKKP). Out of these, works on 468 
water bodies have been completed, while work on the remaining 77 is ongoing. The completion of 468 wat er 
bodies have significantly benefited local communiti es by revival an irrigation potential of 13,010 hec tares 
and restoring, storage capacity of 8.76 M.Cum. Additionally, a noticeable rise in groundwater levels has been 
observed in nearby monitoring wells. Phase-wise details are provided in Annexure. 
To avail central assistance for the Repair, Renovat ion, and Restoration (RRR) of water bodies 
under PMKSY-HKKP, the State Government of Tamil Nad u prepared phase-wise Detailed Project Reports 
(DPRs).  After obtaining clearance/approval from th e State Technical Advisory Committee (STAC) and the  
State-Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC), the propo sals were submitted to the Regional Office of the 
Central Water Commission (CWC), Coimbatore, Tamil N adu, for appraisal. Based on the CWC’s 
recommendations, the Ministry of Jal Shakti made de cisions regarding financial assistance, considering  
factors such as fund availability, feasibility, and regional balance. 
(e) Water being a State subject, the State Governments concerned are mandated to manage and maintain 
the renovated water bodies under their respective j urisdiction. Regular maintenance works for the wate r 
bodies renovated under PMKSY-HKKP are carried out b y the Water Resources Department, Government of 
Tamil Nadu using the annual maintenance funds allocated by the Government of Tamil Nadu.

AREAS OF TAMIL NADU 
 
NO. 4492.  SHRI DURAI VAIKO: 
 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the activities/steps taken/being taken by the Government 
towards sustainable management of groundwater resources in urban 
areas of Tiruchirappalli and Pudukottai districts  in Tamil Nadu during the 
last five years, year and scheme-wise; and 
(b)  the details of the funds allocated and utilised in this regard during the said 
period, year and scheme-wise? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
 
(a) & (b): Water is a S tate subject  and management of water is the 
responsibility of the State Government.  Government of India supplements 
the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ advisories. It 
provides financial and technical support to the States  through various 
schemes/ Missions such as Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT) and AMRUT 2.0. Waterbody rejuvenation is an 
admissible component under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0.  
 
As reported by  the State of  Tamil Nadu on AMRUT Portal , 18 green 
spaces and park projects worth ₹9.33 crore in Pudukottai district and 12 
green spaces and park projects worth ₹8.64 in Tiruchirappalli district were 
taken up under AMRUT Mission and all these projects have been completed.  
 
Under AMRUT 2.0, 12 water body rejuvenation projects worth ₹7.7 
crore and 6 green spaces & park projects worth ₹1.13 crore have been 
approved by MoHUA in Pudukottai district . 14 water body rejuvenation 
projects worth ₹7.45 crore and 13 green spaces & park projects worth ₹2.48 
crore have been approved in Tiruchirappalli district. 
 
Under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0, central funds are allocated/ released to 
States/ Union Territories (UTs) and not to the districts. Funds are utilized by 
the States/UTs as per the progress of the approved projects. Funds released 
by the Ministry and utilisation reported by the State of Tamil Nadu is given 
in Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
Lok Sabha 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 4494 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  27th March 2025 )  
PRODUCTION OF SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL 
4494.    DR. BYREDDY SHABARI                     
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the current status of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) production 
in the country along with the number of SAF pilot projects and test 
flights conducted; 
 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to promote SAF production 
including partnerships with international aviation and fuel 
companies; 
 
(c) the details of challenges faced in SAF production in the country 
along with the measures being taken to address the said 
challenges; 
 
(d) the details of research and development initia tives, 
collaborations or funding provided for the development of SAF in the 
country including the support provided to Indian refineries to 
produce SAF; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to incentivize the 
development and production of SAF in the cou ntry to make it more 
competitive with conventional aviation fuel and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 

(a) to (e) Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) has been used in the 
following test flights:  
i. M/s Vistara operated ferry flight of B -787 from USA to India 
using 28% of SAF blended fuel on 29th March 2023.  
ii. M/s Air Asia operated first commercial domestic flight (Pune to 
Delhi) with 0.75% SAF blended fuel on 19th May 2023.  
iii. M/s Spicejet flight operated with 25% SAF (Biofuel produced by 
Indian Institute of Petroleum, CSIR lab) blended with ATF from 
Dehradun to Delhi in August, 2018.  
iv. All Airbus ferry flights fly on 5% SAF blended fuel from Toulouse 
to India 
; 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG) has informed that 
Public Sector Oil companies are engaged in setting up 
pilot/commercial scale facilities to produce SAF including 
standalone as well as co-processing plants. Production of SAF faces 
challenges such as hig h capital expenditure and operational 
expenditure, expensive feedstock, fragmented supply chains, 
absence of an Indian certification agency for certification and 
sustainability standards, absence of long term off -take agreements 
between Airlines companies and Oil Marketing Companies for 
procurement of SAF, absence of policies support like tax benefits 
and subsidies for SAF production etc. However, envisaged SAF 
plants are expected to catalyze the development of ecosystem for 
domestic SAF production by estab lishing commercial projects and 
setting benchmarks for the development and indigenisation of the 
technologies used for the commercial projects. 
 
The PM JI -VAN Yojana, launched in 2019 and amended in 2024, 
allows grant of financial assistance to set up comm ercial and 
demonstrative advanced biofuel plants including SAF plants. The 
Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 
2027, 2% by 2028, and 5% by 2030 for SAF in ATF, initially for 
international flights.

NO. 4495.  MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the key urban planning initiatives taken/being taken by the Government 
in Tamil Nadu, including Karur Parliamentary Constituency under 
schemes like AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission (SCM) and other urban 
development programmes; 
(b)   the total funds allocated, released and utilized for urban infrastructure 
projects in Tamil Nadu and Karur Parliamentary Constituency under the 
said schemes since 2019; 
(c)  whether the Government has identified any challenges in urban 
planning and development in Tamil Nadu, particularly in tier-2 and tier-
3 cities like Karur and if so, the steps taken to address the same;  
(d) whether there are any pending urban development projects in Karur 
due to delays in funding, approvals or other factors and if so, the 
measures taken/being taken to expedite them; and 
(e) whether the Government has any plans to improve sustainable urban

infrastructure in Tamil Nadu including Karur and if so, the details

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e): As per the provisions of Article 243W of the Constitution, in 
conjunction with the Seventh and Twelfth Schedules, matters relating 
to urban development fall within the purview of States/Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs). However, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) 
provides programmatic support to the State/  Union Territories (UTs) in 
their urban development agenda through its flagship Missions/  
Programmes viz. Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT) & AMRUT 2.0, Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 
(SBM-U) & SBM-U 2.0, Smart Cities Mission (SCM), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) & PMAY-U 2.0, Urban Transport (UT), etc. These 
missions/ schemes/ projects are implemented by the States/UTs in 
accordance with the mission guidelines to improve the ease of living in 
cities and towns covered under these missions. C entral assistance is 
sanctioned to State Governments/UTs and not to the cities. 
…2/ -

AMRUT & AMRUT 2.0:  
AMRUT was launched on 25 June 2015 in selected 500 cities (485 cities 
including 15 merged cities) and towns across the country. The Mission 
focuses on development of basic infrastructure, in the selected cities 
and towns, in the sectors of water supply; sewerage and septage 
management; storm water drainage; green spaces and parks; and non-
motorized urban transport.  A n amount of ₹13,339 crore has been 
sanctioned for these projects  in Tamil Nadu , which includes central 
assistance of ₹4,756.68 crore. 
 
Under AMRUT, 48 projects have been taken up in the Karur 
Parliamentary constituency and an amount of ₹738.58 crore has been 
sanctioned for these projects. Out of these projects, 46 projects worth 
₹25.51 crore have been completed. 
 
Under AMRUT 2.0, a total of 1,270 projects of  ₹14,687.83 crore have 
been approved in Tamil Nadu and 136 projects of ₹1,306.12 crore have 
been approved in Karur Parliamentary constituency.  
 
Under AMRUT, against Central share of ₹4,756.38 crore for projects in 
Tamil Nadu, ₹4,626.24 crore have been released. While under AMRUT 
2.0, against Central share of ₹4,942 crore, ₹1,614.92 crore have been 
released to Tamil Nadu.

Government of India launched the SBM -U on October 2, 2014 with the 
objective of making all cities Open Defecation Free (ODF) and for 100%

urban areas of all States/UTs. To carry forward the progress made, SBM-
U 2.0 has been launched on October 1, 2021 with a vision of achieving 
Garbage Free Status for all cities through 100% source segregation, 
door to door collection and scientific management of all fractions of 
waste including safe disposal in scientific landfills. 
 
Funds are released by Government of India to the States/UTs on the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 4497
(To be answered on the 27th March 2025)
 
AIRPORTS ON RENEWABLE ENERGY
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
 
(a) the percentage of airports currently operating on renewable energy across
the country;
(b) the steps being taken by the Government to make major airports fully
solar or wind-powered;
(c) whether the Government has any plans to mandate renewable energy
adoption for all upcoming airport projects and if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the incentives or policies formulated to encourage private airports to shift
to renewable energy?
 
ANSWER
 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION
 
 
(a): 87 airports out of 159 operational airports i.e. approx. 55% of operational
airports have achieved 100% usage of Green Energy.
 
(b): The airport operators including Airports Authority of India (AAI) have
installed solar power plants at various locations/Airports for generation and
self-consumption of green and renewable energy to encourage green energy
usage at the airports. In addition, few airports are also procuring green
energy through open access. Other initiatives include adoption of building
design as per Green building Standards, conversion of conventional vehicles
to electric vehicles, energy efficient Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning
(HVAC), lighting and baggage handling systems etc.
 
(c) & (d): Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) has advised all the operational
airports with scheduled operations and developers of the upcoming Greenfield
Airports to work towards achieving Carbon Neutrality & Net Zero which
inter-alia includes use of green energy.
 
4497. SHRI K C VENUGOPAL
be pleased to state:-
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol)

MoCA has organised knowledge sharing sessions to standardise Carbon
Accounting and Reporting framework of Indian Airports as well as to create
awareness on Climate Change mitigation. Further, airport operators with
scheduled operations have been advised to map the carbon emission at their
respective airports and to work towards carbon neutrality & net zero
emissions in a phased manner.
 
Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India (AERA) takes into
consideration the Capital expenditure relating to Green Energy Projects,
Carbon Neutrality etc. during the Tariff determination process of Major
Airports.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 4498
(To be answered on the 27th March 2025)
 
PRICE RISE IN AVIATION TURBINE FUEL
 
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
 
(a) the details of the measures being taken by the Government to control the
rising prices of Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF);
(b) whether the Government has taken any steps to reduce the charges levied
at various airports; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
 
ANSWER
 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION
 
 
(a): Taking cognizance of the high value added tax (VAT) on ATF levied by
States/UTs, the issue was taken up with them by Ministry of Civil Aviation
(MoCA). As a result, VAT on ATF has been reduced by 19 States/ UTs. The
States/ UTs which still levy high VAT rates viz. Karnataka, Goa,
Maharashtra, West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Lakshadweep,
Haryana  and Telangana have been requested to reduce VAT rates on ATF.
MoCA has also taken up the issue of extending the GST regime to include
ATF with the Ministry of Finance. Final decision on this matter rests with the
GST Council, where Sates are also represented.
 
(b) & (c): Government of India has established an Independent Economic
Tariff Regulator i.e. Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India
(AERA) in 2009, under the AERA Act, 2008 to determine tariff for
aeronautics service provided at major airports. AERA determines
aeronautical charges such as landing, parking and UDF of all the major
airports, inter-alia considering the following factors :

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4499 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH MARCH, 2025 
  
SETTING UP OF NEW FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
  
4499. SHRI ADHIKARI DEEPAK DEV: 
          SHRI JANARDAN SINGH SIGRIWAL: 
  
          Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to set up new Food Processing Industries at 
the district level across the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Bihar; 
(c) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to set up food processing zones in the 
remaining districts of Bihar; 
(d) the role being played by the Government in the development of food processing parks 
being set up in Bihar; and 
(e) the financial assistance provided to the private entrepreneurs for setting up such units? 
   
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Food Processing industries (MoFPI ) does not setup any food 
processing industries on its own. However, it incentivizes setting up of such industries through 
its Central Sector Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) Scheme, Production 
Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) and Centrally sponsored PM 
Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme across the country 
including Bihar. These schemes are not region or state specific but demand driven and 
applications are invited for financial assista nce through Expression of Interest across the 
country including Bihar. 
 
Under PMKSY, credit linked financial assistance (capital subsidy) is provided to 
entrepreneurs for setting up of food processing industries with total outlay of Rs 5520 Cr for 
15th Finance Commission Cycle.  
 
 
Under PMFME scheme, financial, technical and business support is provided for setting 
up / upgradation of micro food processing enterprises. The scheme is operational for a period 
of upto 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs.10,000 Crore.  
 
 
PLISFPI is, inter alia, intended to support creation of global food manufacturing 
champions and support Indian brands of food products in international market. The Scheme is 
operational for a period from 2021-22 to 2026-27 with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crores.  
 
Mega Food Park and Creation of Infrastructure for Agro -processing Clusters (APC) 
components of PMKSY are aimed at development of such Industries in clusters. The Mega 
Food Park Scheme has been discontinued by the Ministry since 01.04.2021.  Under APC 

Scheme, grants-in-aid @35% of eligible project cost in General Area and grants-in-aid @50% 
of eligible project for projects in Difficult Areas as well as SC/ST, FPOs, SHGs, subject to 
max. of Rs. 10 crore per project  is provided to eligible entrepreneurs. 
 
          The details of food processing industries approved for financial assistance under PMKSY 
and PMFME schemes of MoFPI across the country including Bihar is placed at Annexure.
